text:
incident-bot: 🚨 HIGH — elevated gateway 5xx rate in us-west2 detected. 5m 5xx=4.3% (usual ~0.02%), p99 latency ~1.8s. Affected services: gateway-proxy, transit-router. Paging @alex (oncall). Alert tags: gateway-errors, regional-egress.

alex: on the page, grabbing runbooks. quick ask: are we seeing backend worker oom/killed or just network-level 502/504?

maria: i'm on infra, checking LB health and pod restarts now. initial look: proxy logs show repeated ECONNRESET and upstream 504s to ml-worker pool. no mass pod restarts in the last 30m, but a subset of ml-workers show very high CPU and kernel retransmits.

sam: i'm looking at routing layer — control-plane reports increased connection latencies to us-west2-nat. Could be degraded egress.

alex: ok plan: 1) divert traffic off the most impacted egress pool, 2) scale up fallback pool, 3) throttle or open-circuit noisy callers. maria, can you confirm which pods are hitting retransmits? paste pod names.

maria: copy. running: ```kubectl get pods -n inference | grep worker | grep -E "(us-west2|w-west)"``` output shows: worker-rlk2-5 (CPU 98%), worker-rlk2-9 (CPU 95%, tcp_retrans: 1200/s), worker-rlk2-12 (OK). Also router-proxy-3 showing 502 bursts.

ops-bot: runbook hint: if >2 worker pods show kernel-level retransmits, consider egress NAT pool rehoming and shift traffic regionally.

alex: Maria — please patch the route config to steer 40% traffic from us-west2 -> us-east1 for the next 15m. Use canary weights: us-west2=0.6, us-east1=0.4. Sam, please prepare to cut us-west2 weight to 0 if errors don't drop in 10m.

maria: applying change now: ```routectl set-weights gateway-proxy --region us-west2=0.6 --region us-east1=0.4 --reason "mitigate us-west2 5xx spike"``` returning: OK, rollout id r-20260315-01.

support-bot: customer-impact: detected 12 tenants with >5% error rate in last 10m. Top affected: AcmeCorp (50% of requests failing), BrightCloud (30%), internal-inference-tests. SLA risk flag: true. Notifying CS.

julia: CS ack, I'm drafting a brief to affected customers and will hold until we have stable metrics or an ETA.

alex: good. sam — what telemetry can you surface quickly (p50/p95/p99/how error rate changes)?

sam: pushing graphs to channel: p50 now 180ms -> 350ms, p95 420ms -> 900ms, p99 1.8s -> 2.3s. After weight change we already see 5xx drop from 4.3% -> 2.1% in the 2m window.

maria: launching targeted egress pool rehoming: moving problematic NATs off host-group A -> host-group C. Command: ```infractl nat rehome --pool us-west2-mlworkers --target host-group-c``` Started background job. Logs show connections draining.

alex: also open a temporary circuit for high-frequency clients hitting the workers: add rate-limit 200rps per token for 10m to cut noisy tails.

maria: applying rate-limit rule: ```gatewayctl ratelimit add --matcher "x-customer: highfreq" --limit 200``` done.

ops-bot: suggestion: if errors plateau >1% after 10m, escalate to cross-region failover and consider emergency eviction of the entire worker ASG.

sam: quick health check 5m after steering: 5xx=1.1%, p99=1.0s. Looks promising. We should keep monitoring for 15-20m.

alex: agree. prepare for rollback of weight change if error rate normalizes — keep r-20260315-01 handy. maria, can you attach the rollout to the incident ticket?

maria: attached. also capturing this trace sample showing connection resets to the NAT gateway: ```TRACE id=abc123 path=/v1/generate upstream=10.0.5.9:443 error=ECONNRESET```

support-bot: updated incident timeline and customer list in the ticket: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0315-001 (link). Notifying enterprise CS reps for AcmeCorp and BrightCloud.

julia: sent templated note to impacted customers with status and expected next update in 30m.

sam: metrics stable for 8m post-change, 5xx ~0.9%, some p99 variance but trending down.

alex: i'm going to hand this to on-call infra for continued mitigation and postmortem. @maria @sam — please stay on until handoff complete. escalation: if we see any regression, page SRE lead.

maria: on it. adding notes: probable root cause candidate = NAT host egress degradation causing TCP retransmits to ML worker upstreams; will collect kernel tcpdump and netstat from affected hosts.

alex: thanks team. we will keep traffic steer for 30m and then gradually move back once stable. Postmortem owner: maria. Timeboxed follow-up meeting scheduled in 2 hours.

incident-bot: HANDOFF — incident marked as "stabilized". Handoff to oncall-infra (maria) for investigation and postmortem. Next update window: 30m.

support-bot: final note for now: 0 critical customers in outage; 3 enterprise customers degraded (AcmeCorp high error but mitigation in place). CS sending targeted comms.

alex: closing my active oncall presence, will attend postmortem. Nice triage, team. :thumbsup:
